document.abstract: Digital processing of video signals has become commonplace in television studios. The required electronic components that were state-of-the-art in 1973 are now commodity items. However, the demands placed on the hardware by the processing algorithms have not remained static; the special effects, comb filtering, and bandwidth reduction techniques employed today impose a tremendous computational burden. The real time video signal path needs dedicated, highly pipelined digital circuits. To that end, two integrated circuits have been developed that address the practical problems faced by the video system designer. One, a high speed parallel multiplier, is opitmized for televisions's speed, resolution, accuracy, power, and size constraints. The other, an FIR filter chip, offers an even more efficient solution to the majority of signal filtering applications.

authors.bio: In 1975, Willard K. Bucklen joined TRW Systems Group as an LSI design engineer, where he developed a gate array for the implementation of logic in high-reliability spacecraft computer applications. In 1977 he joined the LSI Products Division and assumed responsibility for the architecture and application of TRW's line of video speed A/D conversion products. He is now the manager of the division's Application Engineering Department. Mr. Bucklen is a member of the SMPTE, IEEE, and Tau Beta Pi.
